summary: This snippet uses Apache's mod_headers module to add a security header that prevents browsers from trying to guess the type of content being served. By setting X-Content-Type-Options to 'nosniff', we're telling the browser 'trust what I tell you this file is, don't try to be clever about it', which prevents certain types of attacks where a malicious file might be misinterpreted.

explanations.1: IfModule checks whether the mod_headers Apache module is installed and enabled; if it's not available, Apache will skip the block inside instead of throwing an error.
explanations.2: Header always set adds an HTTP response header that gets sent to every browser request; 'always' means send it even if there's an error response, and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff tells browsers not to sniff the MIME type of the response.
